parts.label: a
parts.technique: Resultant of forces (vector sum), Newton's second law, magnitude via Pythagoras
parts.reason: Uses addition of forces (M8.5) to find resultant, then Newton's second law for motion in a plane (M8.2/M8.5) and Pythagoras to find magnitude of acceleration; all covered explicitly.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Resultant of forces (vector sum) matching a given direction
parts.reason: Uses addition of forces and resultant direction (M8.5) with vector components; finding p by matching the resultant to a direction vector is straightforward algebra with vectors, which is within the addition-of-forces/resultant topic explicitly covered, no excluded content.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Speed-time graph sketching
parts.reason: Directly covered by M7.2 (graphs in kinematics for motion in a straight line).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Constant acceleration (suvat) formulae
parts.reason: Use of constant acceleration formulae for straight-line motion, explicitly covered by M7.3.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Constant acceleration (suvat) formulae, solving quadratic
parts.reason: Combines the expressions from (b) with total time to solve for V; uses suvat (M7.3) plus quadratic solving (P2.3), both in spec.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Constant acceleration (deceleration) using suvat
parts.reason: Straightforward use of constant acceleration formulae, M7.3.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Impulse–momentum principle
parts.reason: Requires I = m(v-u), i.e. impulse and momentum; impulse is a named mechanics concept not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement (M6.1-M9.1 cover forces, kinematics, moments but not impulse/momentum), so this is out of spec by the 'named concept not mentioned' rule.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Friction (F≤μR) combined with a speed obtained via the out-of-spec impulse calculation
parts.reason: Although friction itself (M8.6) is in spec, this part relies on the speed of P immediately after the impulse from part (a), which is derived from the out-of-spec impulse/momentum concept; since the part only makes sense using that out-of-spec result, it is out.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's experimental law / conservation of linear momentum in collision
parts.reason: Requires collision mechanics (conservation of momentum / Newton's law of impact) which is not covered by any statement in M6-M9; this is a named concept (momentum/collisions) absent from the specification list, so out of spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Moments of forces on a rigid rod (equilibrium)
parts.reason: Directly covered by M9.1 (moments in simple static contexts, rigid bodies).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Moments with an added particle load
parts.reason: Same moments technique as (a), extended with an additional force, still within M9.1.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Moments; point of tilting equilibrium condition
parts.reason: Point of tilting is a standard application of moments equilibrium (M9.1); reaction at one support becomes zero, standard technique within statics of rigid bodies.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Constant velocity vector from position vectors
parts.reason: Uses vectors (P10) and constant velocity kinematics (M7.3/M7.4), both explicitly covered.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Position vector at given time; distance between two points (Pythagoras)
parts.reason: Uses constant velocity model to find position vector, then distance between two points via Pythagoras — covered by M7.3/P10.4.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Resolving forces on inclined plane with friction, equilibrium on point of moving
parts.reason: Covered by M8.4 (equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces, resolving on inclined plane) and M8.6 (friction) guidance explicitly includes inclined-plane problems.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Resolving forces on inclined plane with limiting friction, deriving tan α relation
parts.reason: Combines resolving perpendicular/parallel to plane (M8.4) with F=μR limiting friction model (M8.6); standard technique explicitly supported by guidance on inclined planes.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Comparing maximum friction to weight component to determine equilibrium
parts.reason: Uses the F≤μR model for friction in a static context (M8.6) to justify whether equilibrium is maintained without the string; standard application.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Connected particles over a pulley, Newton's second law
parts.reason: Explicitly covered by M8.4 guidance ('application to problems involving smooth pulleys and connected particles') combined with N2L (M8.2).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Constant acceleration (suvat) using acceleration from connected particles
parts.reason: Uses suvat formula (M7.3) with the acceleration found in (a), which is itself in spec, so full method available in spec.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: suvat for two phases of motion (connected system then free motion under gravity)
parts.reason: First phase uses connected-particle acceleration (M8.4/M7.3); after B lands, A moves freely under gravity, which is straight-line motion under gravity per M8.3/M7.3 — both phases and methods explicitly in spec.
